case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment header.

number_of_accused.reason: Only one accused, the husband appellant, is referred to throughout.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is the husband, referred to as male throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age for the accused appears anywhere in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the accused is not mentioned.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal record of the accused is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is the wife, Raksha Devi, a female.

victim_age.reason: Victim's age is not stated; only marriage and birth dates are given.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused was the victim's husband, so spouse is correct.

offence_category.correct_value: Cruelty by husband (s.498A IPC) and abetment of suicide (s.306 IPC)
offence_category.quote: convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 306 of IPC
offence_category.reason: No culpable homicide charge; offences were cruelty and abetment of suicide.

statutory_provisions.reason: IPC ss.498A and 306 and Evidence Act s.113A are all referred to.

weapon.correct_value: Aluminum phosphide tablets (insecticide), consumed by the victim
weapon.quote: consumed tablets of aluminum phosphide at about 1:45 a.m.
weapon.reason: Judgment identifies the poison used; 'None mentioned' ignores this, though it is not a weapon strictly.

evidence_type.reason: Post-mortem, FIR, witness and circumstantial evidence all feature, though the list is not exhaustive.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused; the victim's suicide note was not exhibited.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Judgment does not expressly list aggravating circumstances for sentencing.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Sessions court convicted under 498A and acquitted under 306, as stated.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court upheld 498A conviction and convicted under 306.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, so the conviction stands.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Cruelty by husband (s.498A IPC) and abetment of suicide (s.306 IPC)
offence_finally_established.quote: convicting the Appellant for the offences under Section 498-A r/w Section 306 of IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Culpable homicide is not an established offence; conviction was under ss.498A and 306.

imprisonment_type.reason: Rigorous imprisonment for a fixed term is stated.

imprisonment_years.quote: rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years ... sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years
imprisonment_years.reason: Five years is correct for s.306 but omits the two-year sentence for s.498A.

fine_rs.quote: pay a fine of Rs.3,000/- ... pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Rs.3,000 is the s.306 fine; the s.498A fine of Rs.1,000 is omitted.

neutral_facts.correct_value: The accused married the victim in 1992 and a male child was born in 1993. The victim filed complaints against the accused, and she died by consuming aluminum phosphide tablets in 1994, within seven years of marriage.
neutral_facts.quote: The High Court vide the impugned Judgment and Order dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellant
neutral_facts.reason: Facts reveal outcomes: High Court conviction, and that the court rejected the defence and found cruelty proved.

offence_severity.reason: Maximum punishments under s.498A (three years) and s.306 (ten years) are stated in the provisions quoted.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: Death after consuming aluminum phosphide tablets is stated.

number_of_offences.reason: Charges under ss.498A and 306 were framed and both upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is mentioned, so 'Not applicable' is consistent with the judgment.

motive.correct_value: Cruelty and harassment by husband, including beatings, driving victim to suicide
motive.quote: the appellant used to beat his wife even when she was pregnant
motive.reason: Judgment identifies cruelty and harassment by the husband as the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Suicide within seven years of marriage (s.113A), proved by consumption of aluminum phosphide, and prior cases of cruelty filed by the victim
key_evidence_accepted.quote: the deceased had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court's finding is 'within seven years'; the value says two years and omits the prior complaints.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Two defence neighbour witnesses were found unconvincing; prosecution witnesses' credibility was not assessed.
witness_credibility.quote: The two defense witnesses claiming to be the neighbours of the appellant ... do not inspire any confidence
witness_credibility.reason: Court only discounted two defence witnesses; main witnesses were not assessed as not credible.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Appellant did not inform the deceased's parents immediately after the incident, which smacked of guilt.
post_offence_conduct.quote: the fact that the appellant had not even bothered to inform the parents of the deceased immediately after the incident smacked of his guilt
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment expressly discusses this post-incident conduct as indicating guilt.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence/death date: 26.09.1994; marriage 10.10.1992; FIR 01.10.1994; sessions judgment 24.02.2000; HC 16.03.2011; SC 23.09.2024
trial_duration.quote: on 26.09.1994 the wife of the appellant Raksha Devi consumed tablets of aluminum phosphide
trial_duration.reason: Marriage date is mislabelled as offence date; the offence date is the death, and FIR date is omitted.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the appearances section.

investigation_status.reason: FIRs 59/1993 and 97/1994, chargesheet and completed trial are all stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Suicide note was not duly exhibited for admission in evidence.
procedural_irregularity.quote: the said suicidal note does not appear to have been duly exhibited for being admitted in evidence
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment notes the suicide note was not duly exhibited, contradicting 'None noted'.

appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.reason: Cruelty, suicide within seven years and s.113A presumption match the prosecution's submissions.

defence_argument.correct_value: Suicide due to victim's pain and illness per suicide note; no cruelty allegations between June 1993 and suicide; no s.113A presumption; conviction based on conjecture.
defence_argument.quote: there were no allegations of cruelty made between the period June 1993 till she committed suicide
defence_argument.reason: Omits the no-cruelty and conjecture arguments and attributes the court's own findings on the note and parents to the defence.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Section 113A discretionary presumption of abetment is correctly identified.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Hans Raj and Naresh Kumar citations match the footnotes.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Not stated; the court gives no sentencing reasoning, only the basis for conviction (cruelty and abetment).
sentencing_rationale.quote: We therefore, do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned order
sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment gives reasons for conviction, not for the sentence imposed.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are discussed, so 'None' is consistent.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: No aggravating factors are expressly identified for sentencing.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Fine with default clause for both the s.498A and s.306 sentences.
other_sentence_order.quote: pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- with the default clause
other_sentence_order.reason: Default clauses attached to both fines are omitted; 'None' understates the sentence orders.
